classification.difficultyReason: Combine shape features, adjacency and repeated side markings to resolve correspondence in rotated or reflected figures, then encode the complete matching order in a congruence statement.

content.prompt:
Write a congruence statement for these shapes.
Remember that the matching vertices should be in the same order.

spec.description: Paired triangles with opposite vertical orientations; all six vertex labels retained.
spec.mathematics: CA and EF are vertical; AB and ED are horizontal. Correspondence A–E, B–D, C–F.
spec.answerVisibility: Vertex labels and outlines are permanent givens; the congruence statement is a controlled response.

answer.worked: The corresponding vertices are $A\leftrightarrow E$, $B\leftrightarrow D$ and $C\leftrightarrow F$. Hence $\Delta ABC\equiv\Delta EDF$.

spec.description: Paired trapeziums with reversed upper and lower short sides.
spec.mathematics: AB corresponds to YX; BC to XW; CD to WZ; DA to ZY.
spec.answerVisibility: All vertex labels and outlines are permanent givens.

answer.worked: Match the short parallel sides $AB$ and $YX$, then the adjacent vertical sides $BC$ and $XW$. The corresponding order is $A\leftrightarrow Y$, $B\leftrightarrow X$, $C\leftrightarrow W$, $D\leftrightarrow Z$, so $ABCD\equiv YXWZ$.

spec.description: Oppositely oriented triangles with meaningful horizontal extensions AB and XW.
spec.mathematics: A, B, C are collinear in that order; Z, X, W are collinear in that order. A–W, B–X, C–Z, D–Y correspond under a half-turn.
spec.answerVisibility: All extensions and labels are permanent givens.

answer.worked: A half-turn matches the extension $AB$ with $WX$ and triangle $BCD$ with triangle $XZY$. Thus $A\leftrightarrow W$, $B\leftrightarrow X$, $C\leftrightarrow Z$, $D\leftrightarrow Y$, giving $ABCD\equiv WXZY$.

spec.description: Paired pentagons retaining all single and double side ticks.
spec.mathematics: EA, AB, BC and XZ, ZT, TW have single ticks. CD, DE and WS, SX have double ticks. Correspondence A–T, B–Z, C–X, D–S, E–W.
spec.answerVisibility: Side ticks and labels are permanent givens.

answer.worked: Match the vertices while preserving the order of the single- and double-marked sides: $A\leftrightarrow T$, $B\leftrightarrow Z$, $C\leftrightarrow X$, $D\leftrightarrow S$, $E\leftrightarrow W$. Hence $ABCDE\equiv TZXSW$.

spec.description: Paired concave quadrilaterals with marked vertices and one-, two- and three-tick sides.
spec.mathematics: Concave vertices N and S correspond. MN–TS have two ticks; NO–SQ one; OP–QR and PM–RT three.
spec.answerVisibility: All points, side ticks and labels are permanent givens.

answer.worked: The inward vertices correspond: $N\leftrightarrow S$. Matching the adjacent double- and single-marked sides gives $M\leftrightarrow T$ and $O\leftrightarrow Q$, leaving $P\leftrightarrow R$. Therefore $MNOP\equiv TSQR$.

spec.description: Paired quadrilaterals with vertical sides, filled vertices, right-angle squares and internal single/double angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: A and B correspond to H and G; D's single arc corresponds to E's; C's double arc corresponds to F's. The interior obtuse sectors at C and F carry the double arcs.
spec.answerVisibility: All angle marks, points and labels are permanent givens.

answer.worked: The single arcs give $D\leftrightarrow E$ and the double arcs give $C\leftrightarrow F$. The adjacent right-angle vertices then match as $B\leftrightarrow G$ and $A\leftrightarrow H$. Hence $ABCD\equiv HGFE$.
